newsitem.title: USA: 76-year-old bomb victim says he needs a cure for stupidity.
newsitem.headline: 76-year-old bomb victim says he needs a cure for stupidity.

text.p: John Morton had only one request when he arrived at an Atlanta hospital after being caught in Thursday's double-bomb blast outside a local abortion clinic.
"I asked the nurses down there if they had a pill to cure stupidity," the 76-year-old man joked afterwards.

Upon hearing that a bomb had exploded at the Atlanta Northside Family Planning Services centre, he decided to wander down to the facility from his nearby Sandy Springs home -- ignoring his wife's instructions to stay away.
Morton said in an interview with NBC affiliate WXIA-TV that he intended to offer his help to friends in the local fire department who had been called to the site.
But as he stood surveying the scene, a second bomb detonated near a garbage container in the corner of the building's parking lot.
"There was a blue car and I happened to notice that the windscreen was all cracked. And just then, boom!" he recalled.
His injuries amounted to no more than some small scratches on his head and a pair of ringing ears.
But Morton, a retired Army munitions expert, also had some well-informed advice for investigators who began a second day combing through the site for evidence Friday.

"It was a high-order explosive, probably a plastic explosive of some kind," the jaunty septuagenarian surmised after emerging from Grady Memorial Hospital with his flat cap perched squarely atop a head bandage.
"That's terrorism. They know they're going to try to make casualties," he added.
"We must get these people, give them a proper trial and a prompt execution, because they are multiple killers," he said.
